name: Mole
tagline: Native Mac utility for cleanup, software, and status.
description:
Mole is a Mac maintenance utility that brings cleanup, application removal, storage analysis, and live system information into one tool. Its approach is review-first, so the user can inspect what will change before deleting files or altering system-maintenance data.

It is useful when a Mac feels cluttered but Finder does not reveal the cause. You can look for old caches and logs, inspect large files and folders, remove an app together with its leftovers, or check whether CPU, memory, storage, battery, or network activity explains a slowdown.

Mole combines jobs that many people otherwise spread across a cleaner, an uninstaller, a disk visualizer, and a menu bar monitor. That breadth is convenient, but it also makes careful review essential because cleanup tools can remove data that a user may want to keep.

## Features

- Review and remove caches, logs, browser remnants, and other temporary files to reclaim storage without treating cleanup as an automatic black box.
- Uninstall applications together with related preferences, launch agents, and support files that macOS may leave behind.
- Map disk usage and locate large files or folders before deciding what should be removed.
- Monitor CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network, battery, and fan activity from Mole’s system-status tools.
- Run selected maintenance tasks such as rebuilding caches or Quick Look data when a specific Mac behavior calls for them.
- Use the open-source command-line tool or the native Mac interface, depending on whether you prefer scripts or visual review.

## Where it fits

Mole suits people who want a transparent alternative to a collection of separate Mac-maintenance utilities. It is particularly useful for occasional cleanup, uninstalling stubborn apps, and understanding storage or system activity.

It should not be used as a routine “fix everything” button. Deleting caches and support files requires judgment, and users who only need one focused job may prefer a dedicated uninstaller, disk visualizer, or system monitor.
